F1.evidence: crates/aspis-core/src/r0/heap.rs:5-10 (filled: try_reserve_exact -> Err(Allocation)), :11-14 (uninit); callers candidate.rs:256 (prepare), verifier.rs:93 (Accumulator::new), verifier.rs:207 (BatchedWeights::new), verifier.rs:428 (resume, TX2:064), r1_semantic.rs:45 (claims). The CLOSED roots quantify the reservation (NKA_ClaimsRoot.claims: allocator/state/reservation; NGC/NIG filled roots: reservation; NKH caller clause: both arms).
F1.consequence: RSL.Env carries sha256/pda/clock only, so a fallible reservation outcome is not an oracle reply. A faithful Child law for these fields must admit both Ok and Err(Allocation) at the same arguments and Env, and impl : Args -> Env -> Obs cannot be the actual function. The RowSpec proofs are unaffected (a relational law admits the impl), but the TX1 returned path 345->328->094->087->filled/accNew/weightsNew and 136->claims becomes nondeterministic at fixed Env, so AMN.a1_forces_det makes A1 (NND_A1/A1min Err arm) and NND_Tx1ReturnedValues.returned unprovable; TX2 tx2auth gives the same for NND_Tx2Values.auth_ret. The rev2 header claim that the only nondeterminism is the aborting allocation site is false for try_reserve sites.
F1.recommendation: lead applies a rev2 patch: add a quantified reservation reply to RSL.Env (ruling (at) shape, one reply per fallible site occurrence), make the four VLib children and the 064 law read it, and bind it in Sig.EnvRep to the headline reservation binder. Alternative (worse): an owner ruling that try_reserve failure is outside the obligation, which would be a trust addition. LIB builds every other field now and leaves these five behind a parameter until the lead rules.

F2.evidence: TX1:179 root NHS_PreparedPacket.source has premise compact_check : check_values compact = ok (Ok ()) on the 464-byte y1 slice; ledger 179 inventory domain says "LPt compact464 checked". Frozen prepare (candidate.rs:255-264) runs expand_values (compact.rs:127-136, no canonicality check) and never calls check_values; only tx1 calls canonical_scan (candidate.rs:275) before prepare. RowSpec_087 Domain is R1-R3 only. NMP_REMAINING records the same gap ("179 canonicality").
F2.consequence: With P.dom verbatim from 179 (the RSL rule), RowSpec_087 is unprovable: the parent cannot discharge the child domain at the call.
F2.recommendation: add own-input clause (R4) "proof[7031..7495] passes check_values" to RowSpec_087, discharged in RowSpec_094 from the TX1:084 canonical_scan law at SAME proof. This narrows 087 only and does not propagate past 094.
